interpretation: If (a) holds, the degeneracy gate is necessary: a 'reliable' degenerate model cannot discriminate correct from incorrect movement. If (b) holds, cross-exercise rank consistency (Kendall W) is a usable validity proxy. Together they upgrade the reliability rubric from self-consistency to a validated deployment screen.

external_transfer.interpretation: KIMORE-trained scorers do NOT transfer zero-shot to correct/incorrect discrimination: best per-exercise AUROC over all models x all 5 exercise embeddings = 0.533. Naive movement-magnitude features on the SAME joint-mapped sequences reach mean|AUROC| = 0.647, so the label signal is present and the joint mapping is sound -- the failure is model transfer, not the testbed. The reliability/degeneracy diagnostic is thus validated as a NECESSARY screen-out (degenerate -> chance) but is NOT sufficient for validity: high zero-shot reliability does not imply a model can flag movement errors on an external labeled set.
